# row echelon form　`def.row-echelon-form`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.row-echelon-form)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.row-echelon-form.md)

**Theorem (elimination)**: every $A \in M_{m \times n}(K)$ can be brought to reduced row echelon form by finitely many elementary row operations, and this reduced row echelon form is **unique**. The number of pivots equals $\operatorname{rank} A$.

## Notes · **draft**
Uniqueness is the point of RREF: row echelon form is not unique (one may continue performing row operations), but "pivots equal to $1$, all other entries in pivot columns zero" removes every degree of freedom and leaves exactly one form.
